Sandbagging by a password-locked model could potentially be uncovered by estimating the capability scaling of the algorithm code through small experiments using known data sets. This approach could allow for the estimation of the scaling law for the algorithm, which might help in detecting attempts at sandbagging.

Standard capability elicitation might fail to reveal the sandbagging because the password locking of the model could be so effective that there are no hints of the dangerous capabilities. If the capabilities are locked behind a password that is not known to the evaluator, the evaluation results might appear reasonable, and the capability elicitation efforts may not yield any signals to boost, making it difficult to detect the hidden capabilities.
